newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican labor boss leaves hospital -- doctor.
newsitem.headline: Mexican labor boss leaves hospital -- doctor.

text.p: Mexico's 96-year-old labor leader Fidel Velazquez left the hospital on Tuesday four weeks after being admitted for a recurring intestinal infection, his doctor said Tuesday.
"He was given permission to leave today and has returned to his home in Lomas," Dr. Salomon Jasqui said, referring to one of Mexico City's plush western suburbs.

Velazquez is head of the six-million-strong Mexican Workers Confederation (CTM), an umbrella organisation for most of Mexico's unions, and a stalwart supporter of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).
Jasqui said he did not know when Velazquez, who turns 97 on April 24, would return to work, but he said he could resume light duties "in a few days after a period of rest."
Velazquez, who has helped keep a lid on worker unrest for half a century, has been hospitalized at least three times in the last five months.
